summary:
**AstroVital – Project Summary**

AstroVital is an AI-powered health-monitoring platform designed to support astronaut well-being during space missions.

It addresses spaceflight-related health challenges, including cardiovascular changes, immune alterations, sleep disturbances, and fatigue.

The platform integrates three types of health data:

1. **Physiological:** Heart rate, SpO₂, blood pressure, and other available measurements.
2. **Biochemical:** Periodic laboratory measurements, including CBC and selected immune biomarkers.
3. **Behavioral:** Sleep quality, physical activity, and fatigue indicators.

Using personalized health baselines, trend analysis, and AI-driven anomaly detection, AstroVital identifies unusual patterns, explains changes, and provides understandable alerts and follow-up guidance.

The platform draws on NASA research resources, including the Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), and uses simulated telemetry where applicable.

Its web-based dashboard visualizes health trends and supports astronaut self-assessment and informed medical review.

**Our vision: Transform isolated health measurements into personalized health intelligence for safer, long-duration space missions.**
details:
Background & Literature Review NASA's Human Research Program (HRP) identifies five major hazards associated with human spaceflight and conducts ongoing research to understand their effects on astronaut health. These hazards provide the scientific foundation for selecting relevant health indicators and developing monitoring strategies. NASA research addresses physiological and behavioral risks involving cardiovascular adaptation, hypoxia, immune-system changes, nutrition, sleep, and behavioral health. The Canadian Space Agency (CSA) also contributes to astronaut health protection through radiation monitoring and exposure assessment programs. Scientific research further supports individualized and longitudinal health monitoring. Studies involving astronauts have demonstrated the importance of tracking biological and physiological changes over time rather than relying exclusively on population-wide reference values. AstroVital builds upon these research directions by combining personalized health baselines, repeated measurements, transparent classification rules, and accessible guidance. Unlike complex clinical research platforms, AstroVital focuses on providing a practical, crew-facing interface that supports health awareness and preventive decision-making. The system is designed as a decision-support prototype and does not replace professional medical evaluation. Methodology A. Step-by-Step Process Step 1 — Scientific Research and Indicator Selection. Studied NASA HRP's five hazards and ongoing research, together with CSA radiation-monitoring resources, to identify relevant health indicators: • Sleep quality and duration • Fatigue • Resting pulse • Blood oxygen saturation (SpO2 ) • Blood pressure • Mood • Nutrition • Physical exercise • Body temperature Step 2 — Personalized Health Baselines. Established an individual health baseline for each crew member using their own first week of recorded measurements. This allows the system to identify deviations from an astronaut's normal physiological patterns rather than relying exclusively on general population thresholds. Step 3 — Deterministic Rules Engine. Each new health check-in is processed through a deterministic rules engine that classifies the result into four categories: • Green: Measurements are within the expected range. • Yellow: A potential deviation requires attention or monitoring. • Red: An explicit critical symptom or configured emergency limit has been detected. • Grey: Data are missing or outdated. Step 4 — Personalized Guidance Cards. Each finding is converted into a plain-language, symbol-first card containing: what changed; why it matters; what action to take; when to recheck; and when to contact medical support.

Step 5 — Closed-Loop Action Tracking. The astronaut can start and complete recommended actions, with each action recorded in the health timeline. When a Red event occurs, the system generates a structured onboard report. The report remains queued until a simulated communication uplink and acknowledgement are completed. Step 6 — Testing and Verification. The system's behavior was verified through 11 engine tests and a UI smoke test covering all scenarios. B. Algorithms and Technologies Technology stack: Python, Streamlit, pandas, NumPy, Plotly. The application runs locally and fully offline without requiring an external API key. Personal Baseline Algorithm: The system uses the median and Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) to establish robust individual health reference ranges. Persistence Detection: A signal must remain outside its expected range in at least 3 of the last 4 entries before being considered persistent. For SpO2 , the requirement is 2 of the last 4 entries. Multi-Signal Detection: Recovery drift requires at least two abnormal indicators among sleep, fatigue, and resting pulse. The system identifies co-occurring changes without claiming that one indicator directly causes another. Outlier Detection: A single outlier is flagged for retesting at 3 robust standard deviations rather than automatically being interpreted as a persistent health issue. Emergency Classification: Red classification is triggered only by explicitly configured emergency criteria or critical symptoms. Missing Data Management: Grey classification is used when measurements are missing or stale. Guidance System: A local, source-linked guidance library provides relevant information and recommendations. No AI model makes medical decisions. C. Fit With the Challenge AstroVital supports astronaut self-assessment through an intuitive visual interface combining color, shape, and written status indicators. The platform provides: • Interactive body mapping • Personalized health trend charts • Preventive health guidance • Flight-surgeon escalation pathways • Offline functionality during communication delays • Gamification to encourage consistent monitoring • An evidence library connected to NASA and CSA resources Solution AstroVital is a web-based astronaut health dashboard that transforms physiological measurements and behavioral observations into understandable, personalized health information. The solution consists of several integrated components: • 1. Health Monitoring Dashboard — a centralized overview of the astronaut's health indicators and current status. • 2. Personalized Baseline Engine — establishes individual reference values and identifies unusual changes over time. • 3. Health Classification Engine — assigns Green, Yellow, Red, or Grey classifications using transparent rules.

• 4. Interactive Guidance System — personalized action cards explaining detected changes and recommended next steps. • 5. Health Timeline — records check-ins, alerts, completed actions, and health events. • 6. Onboard Medical Reporting — generates structured reports for critical events and keeps them queued until simulated communication becomes available. • 7. Evidence Library — scientific context and source-linked guidance based on NASA, CSA, and relevant research. Implementation Process • Collecting health check-ins and simulated wearable telemetry • Establishing personal baselines • Processing measurements through the rules engine • Displaying classifications and health trends • Providing appropriate guidance • Recording actions and health events • Testing the complete workflow, including emergency reporting and communication delays The current prototype uses simulated wearable telemetry to demonstrate continuous monitoring. Value Proposition AstroVital provides value by transforming complex health measurements into understandable and actionable information. For astronauts, the platform offers a simple way to monitor personal health trends, recognize unusual changes, and understand recommended actions. For mission medical teams, it provides structured health records, documented events, and organized reports that can be reviewed when communication becomes available. Its main advantages include: • Personalization: Each astronaut is monitored against their own baseline. • Transparency: Classifications are based on understandable deterministic rules. • Offline Capability: Operates without continuous internet connectivity. • Preventive Monitoring: Persistent deviations can be identified before they meet emergency criteria. • Action Tracking: Recommended actions and their completion are documented. • Scientific Foundation: Guidance is connected to NASA and CSA resources. • Communication Resilience: Critical reports can remain queued during communication delays. Unlike conventional dashboards that primarily display raw measurements, AstroVital connects monitoring with interpretation, guidance, and action tracking. It is designed to complement existing medical monitoring systems and professional medical judgment, not replace them. Role of Team Members • Remon Asaad — Research & Database. Scientific research, identifying relevant NASA and CSA resources, studying astronaut health indicators, organizing scientific references, and managing the project's database and evidence-linked guidance library. • Mahmoud Ahmed Hussein — Storytelling. Project storytelling, communicating the problem and proposed solution, developing the presentation narrative, and ensuring health information and recommendations are communicated clearly and effectively. • Abdulrahman Mahmoud — Technical Development. Technical implementation, application development, integrating the health-monitoring engine, data processing, the Streamlit interface, visualizations, and software testing.
